correctness.rationale: Choose a maximizing Fourier frequency χ₀ and demodulate. The finite transitive affine average sends the demodulated function g to h=c·1_S, with c nonzero because the maximizing coefficient is nonzero. Affine pullbacks induce isometries of counting Fourier ℓʳ (phase and permutation). Their average H=ĥ has norm (1−δ)R for R=||f̂||ᵣ, in particular justifying δ∈[0,1). The pairwise convexity inequality has exponent s=r and coefficient β=1 for r>2, and s=2, β=r−1 for 1<r<2. Averaging over two independent translates of ĝ bounds the expected s-th power of their difference by (2ˢ/β)(Rˢ−||H||ᵣˢ): Jensen bounds the expected midpoint norm power below by ||H||ᵣˢ. Isometry and uniform group measure reduce the two-translate difference to one relative translate; Jensen then bounds ||ĝ−H||ᵣˢ by that one-translate expectation. At r=2 the average is an orthogonal projection, giving the stated identity. The singleton case has δ=0 and equality. For r>2, the full-support two-frequency example has δ∼tʳ/r and best relative error t/(1+tʳ)^(1/r). For 1<r≤2, on {0,1} in Z₃ the nonmaximal Fourier magnitudes before the common normalization are sqrt(1+3t²), with maximizing magnitude 2 for small t. Thus δ=3t²/(2ʳ+2)+Oᵣ(t⁴). The perturbation is transverse to the trivial modulation line while the two other lines are separated from the limiting signal; the best relative error is bounded below by a constant times |t|. Both obstructions are to any higher exponent even on the respective fixed group and support.
residual_risks: The supplied sanity tests are not independent execution evidence; the result follows by analytic inequalities and exact small examples.
Iosevich–Li–Yu state the exact-constant theorem on Z_N^d; the proof of the reviewed bound supplies the requisite extension to general finite abelian groups directly by affine averaging.

evidence: Ricard–Xu give the general conditional expectation estimate for 1<p≤2 and the general two-point inequality; known uniform convexity gives the power type of the upper estimates. The Bhowmik–Deodhar–Iosevich Theorem 5 gives a finite spectral-synthesis inequality, not a near-equality stability statement.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Indeed, the averaged orbit vector may be lifted to the product of the finite symmetry group and the Fourier coordinate set, with normalized measure on the group, so Ricard–Xu's expectation inequality implies a stronger upper constant for 1<r≤2. A general upper estimate or even its sharp abstract power does not settle optimality on the restricted Fourier-supported affine-transitive families with minimization over all modulations. The two explicit restricted extremizer perturbations do that.

value.rationale: This answers the stated Fourier near-equality question in a concrete norm, uniformly in group size and support, and proves that the powers cannot improve even on fixed small groups when the comparison extremizer is optimized. The meaningful contribution is the optimal Fourier-specific stability law and its two distinct obstruction regimes, not novelty of convexity or optimality of the displayed constants.
residual_risks: Scope is Fourier ℓʳ for 1<r<∞ with transitive support symmetry, not a general time-domain or endpoint stability theorem.
